speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to help me determine the cause, have you noticed any recent insect bites, travel to specific areas, or contact with others who are ill?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).

The combination of a prodrome of fever and rhinorrhea followed by a pruritic rash that spares the perioral area is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. Given the patient's age and the specific description of the facial rash, no further diagnostic testing is required at this time.
